hook: This red bell is built to pull sailors out of a sunken submarine.
narration: This red bell is built to pull sailors out of a sunken submarine.
It is the Navy's Submarine Rescue Chamber, training off Catalina Island, California.
The crew climbs in through the top hatch, and the bell goes over the side.
It rides down to the sub and seals itself over the escape hatch.
On this dive it went to ninety feet and locked onto a fake submarine hatch.
In a real rescue, it can go as deep as eight hundred fifty feet.
The same kind of bell saved thirty three men from the sunken submarine Squalus, in 1939.
outcome: The bell came back to the surface, and the hatch on top swung open.
title: The bell that rescues sunken sub crews
description:
The Navy's Undersea Rescue Command trained with its Submarine Rescue Chamber off Catalina Island, California, in 2015, diving to 90 feet to mate with a fixture that simulates a submarine hatch.

facts.claim: URC trains with the SRC off Catalina Island
facts.source_quote: Undersea Rescue Command (URC) conducts Submarine Rescue Chamber (SRC) training operations aboard HOS Dominator off the coast of Catalina Island

facts.claim: Dived to 90 feet, mated with a fixture simulating a sub hatch, returned to the surface
facts.source_quote: The SRC dives to 90 feet and mates with a portable training fixture simulating a submarine hatch before returning to the surface.
The SRC conducts shallow water rescues, diving to a maximum depth of 850 feet.
